masa: [Mana+sa] (na) CL=7 [Moga,7.213. Dhāna,ṭī.157. Masa+a. Vinayālaṅkāra,ṭī,1.78. Māna+sa. Pācita, Yo.70] The meat. There are ten kinds of meat that Bhikkhus are not allowed to eat.  (according to Vinaya), The flesh of humans, elephants, horses, dogs, snakes, lions, tigers, leopards, bears, and yaks. If a Bhikkhu eats the flesh of people, he commits a Thullaccaya āpatti. If a Bhikkhu eats the other nine kinds of meat, he commits a dukkaṭa Āpatti. Vi,3.312-4. Also not permitted are the bone, blood, skin, and hair of these kinds of unallowable meats. Vi, ṭṭha, 3. 376. If a Bhikkhu doesn"t the type of meat, or the time, he should ask.  Except for these ten kinds of meat, the other meat can eat if free from three factors. Vi,ṭṭha,2.189.191. (See - Tikoṭiparisuddha for these three factors). See original.
